validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented FERC Natural Gas Act project. Double E Pipeline, LLC filed a prior-notice request under its blanket certificate (Docket CP19-495-000) on 2022-12-09 for the Red Hills Lateral -- 20 mi of 24-in lateral pipeline, Poker Lake Meter Station to a new Red Hill meter station, Eddy/Lea Counties NM, ~$35.8M -- authorized under Docket CP23-24-000 effective 2023-02-18 (Federal Register 87 FR 78950, 2022-12-23, FR Doc 2022-27975; confirmed independently by the EIA Historical Projects release). Correctly classified gas transmission lateral (NGA-jurisdictional interstate facility), not oil, not gathering. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the cluster warning (P5727 and P7830 both titled 'Double E Pipeline Project'): NOT a duplicate. P5727 is the Red Hills Lateral (docket CP23-24, filed Dec 2022). This row's own harvested gem.wiki citation list (footnotes 13-16 on the wiki page) cites four 2011-2014 news items about an entirely different 'Double E' -- a Cushing-to-Houston CRUDE OIL pipeline dispute between Enterprise Products and Energy Transfer Partners, unrelated to Double E Pipeline, LLC's Permian gas system. The batch prompt independently pre-characterizes P7830 as an 'Original Proposal (Oil Pipeline), cancelled 2011' -- consistent with this being the same coincidentally-named 2011 oil dispute, not an earlier phase or duplicate entry of the current gas project. Filed as a cross_row_leads entry below (oil is out of scope this cycle; not researching P7830 itself per the batch prompt's explicit instruction). Also not a duplicate of the P0061 mainline (swept in slice 1) or of the mainline expansion EIA record ('Double E Pipeline Expansion', May2026 release) -- Red Hills Lateral is its own FERC docket and its own physical lateral, now cancelled. DEFECT FOUND (documented, not actioned as a fill): the EIA Aug2026 Historical Projects row for 'Red Hills Lateral Project' carries a 'website' field pointing to https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-05-03/pdf/2024-09686.pdf -- fetched and read via pdftotext; that Federal Register page (89 FR 36808-36809) is actually 'Carlsbad Gateway, LLC; ... Docket No. CP24-200-000', an unrelated Targa Resources 'Lea County Expansion Project' (Targa's Red Hills Processing Plant to the Agua Blanca Pipeline) that only coincidentally shares the place-name 'Red Hills'. This citation was NOT used as a ref anywhere in this shard. AUTO-COMPARISON CORRECTION: this row's own prompt auto-generated a comparison table against the mainline 'Double E Pipeline' EIA record (1350 MMcf/d, 133.8 mi, docket CP19-495) and flagged every field as 'differs' from the sheet (600 vs 1350 MMcf/d, 20 vs 133.8 mi, etc.) -- that comparison used the WRONG EIA candidate (the parent trunk, not the segment). The prompt's own '[strong]' Red Hills Lateral Project EIA candidate (docket CP23-24, 20 mi/24 in/600 MMcf/d/$35.8M) matches the sheet's recorded values exactly once matched to the correct EIA row -- the sheet's specs were never actually in conflict. STATUS: see status_reviews -- EIA's Aug2026 release recodes this project Cancelled (FERC denied Double E's construction-deadline extension 2024-03-21); the sheet's recorded 'proposed' is stale. [Orchestrator 2026-09-15: this record carried tier=high / independent=true with an EMPTY proposed_refs list. Validity records carry no verifications[] by repo convention, so the tier is counted over proposed_refs and an empty list reads as zero publishers. Staged the two origins the note above already rests on and which are verified elsewhere on this shard: the Federal Register notice of 2022-12-23 (87 FR 78950, FR Doc 2022-27975) for the existence, docket and physical description, and the EIA Aug2026 release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects') for the independent corroboration and the cancellation. Two distinct publishers, so high/independent stands on evidence. The govinfo.gov PDF discussed above is deliberately NOT staged -- it is the mis-citation this record reports, not a source for it.]

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Sheet's LastUpdated is 2025-10-15 and its current ref (2024-02-12 Federal Register notice) only records Double E's REQUEST for a one-year extension (filed 2024-01-31, requesting until 2025-02-18); it does not reflect the outcome. EIA's tracked history of this project (15 releases, 2023-01 through 2026-08) shows the status progression Applied (2023-01 to 2024-01) -> Approved (2024-04, 2024-07) -> Approved/On Hold (2024-10, 2025-01, 2025-04) -> Completed (2025-07, anomalous -- likely a data-entry artifact given the subsequent reversal) -> Cancelled (2025-10 onward, carried through the 2026-01, 2026-05 and 2026-08 releases). The Aug 2026 release's project_notes are explicit and dated: FERC denied Double E's extension request on 2024-03-21, meaning the authorized one-year construction window (2023-02-18 to 2024-02-18) lapsed without an approved extension. This is a single-origin (EIA) finding -- I could not independently verify the 2024-03-21 denial order itself: FERC eLibrary is JS-only/unscrapable via curl and no Federal Register notice was ever published announcing the denial (agencies only publish FR notices for filings requiring public comment, not for orders disposing of them); an extensive Google News RSS search for 'Red Hills Lateral' / 'Double E' cancellation turned up no press coverage. Circumstantial corroboration: Double E filed an entirely new docket (CP26-542-000, 'Dude Lateral Project', filed 2026-06-11 -- Federal Register 91 FR 38411, 2026-06-25) for a near-identical 22.1-mile, 20-inch lateral in the same two counties (Eddy/Lea) for the same stated purpose (access to Delaware Basin supplies) -- consistent with Red Hills Lateral having been abandoned and effectively replaced by a re-filed project, rather than merely stalled. Recommend Status=cancelled, ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed (evidence-based, not dormancy-inferred) at medium tier; a CancelledYear=2024 could also be set from the same EIA source if the schema calls for one (not included in proposed_changes above since it was not in this row's worklist units, but noted here for the merge step).

cross_row_leads.facts: This row's own gem.wiki reference list (citations 13-16, harvested for P5727) includes four 2011-2014 news items -- resolved from their original bit.ly short links -- about an entirely different 'Double E': a Cushing, OK-to-Houston, TX CRUDE OIL pipeline capacity dispute between Enterprise Products Partners and Energy Transfer Partners (open commitment period announced May 2011; ETP sued Enterprise and Enbridge in 2011; a Dallas jury awarded ETP $319 million in a 'common law partnership' verdict in March 2014, per this Dallas News article and a companion Reuters piece). This is NOT the same entity as Double E Pipeline, LLC (the FERC-regulated Permian gas transmission company behind P5727/P0061), and predates it by roughly a decade. The batch prompt independently characterizes P7830 as an 'Original Proposal (Oil Pipeline)' cancelled in 2011 -- consistent with P7830 actually describing this unrelated, coincidentally-named 2011 crude-oil dispute/proposal rather than an earlier phase or duplicate of the current gas project. Recommend the P7830 researcher weigh whether P7830 belongs in the gas tracker at all (oil is out of scope this cycle; not researched further here per the batch prompt's explicit instruction not to research, stage, or propose anything for the oil tracker).
